architecture_notes: Single crate (rust-workspace-map v0.2.0, edition 2024). No new crates or modules introduced.
All changes fit in existing files: src/schema.rs, src/indexes.rs, src/validate.rs, README.md, tests/fixtures/bad-orphan/, tests/integration_test.rs.

G1 and G2 both modify check_dead_reexports in validate.rs. G1 adds a pre-check at the top of the per-re-export loop; G2 adds logic in the !symbols.contains_key branch. They touch different regions but share the same function body — implement sequentially (G1 first, then G2) to avoid merge conflicts.
SymbolEntry uses #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]. The new derive_attrs field will serialize as "deriveAttrs" in JSON output. This is consistent with all other SymbolEntry fields.
derive_attrs values are pre-sorted by extract_attrs (file_parser.rs line 481: derive.sort()). No additional sorting needed.
SymbolEntry uses bon::Builder. The new derive_attrs field must carry #[builder(default)] so existing builder call sites that omit it continue to compile.
All BTreeMap-based collections are sorted by key for deterministic output.

The existing cross-crate check at lines 148-151 of validate.rs (checking first_seg against crate_names) MUST NOT be removed. It handles cross-workspace-member re-exports that pass the G1 pre-check. G1 short-circuits before this check for external-crate paths; the existing check remains as a safety net for cross-workspace-member paths.
Paths throughout the codebase are workspace-relative strings. No absolute paths introduced.
Error handling: all new functions are pure predicates returning bool. No Result, no panics. Use early returns and conditionals.
Naming conventions: snake_case functions (is_*, check_*), descriptive variable names, test_<scenario> for tests.
Unit tests live in #[cfg(test)] mod tests within the same file. Integration tests invoke the compiled binary via std::process::Command.

Library code in this phase follows ch12-04 TDD: tests claim interfaces first via tdd_interface, then implementations evolve to meet them. See /Users/tony/programming/rust-development-pipeline/skills/elaborate-directions/references/tdd-pattern.md for the reference pattern.
known_pitfalls: G1: crate_names alone is insufficient for bare-path check. A bare path like 'use utils::Helper' where 'utils' is both a workspace member name AND a top-level module of the current crate must be treated as internal (NOT skipped). Must also check crate_info.modules for top-level modules of the current crate.

G1: The existing cross-crate check (lines 148-151 of validate.rs) operates on resolved paths. G1 operates on the original unresolved import_path. They coexist: G1 runs first and short-circuits via continue for external crates; the existing check remains as a safety net for cross-workspace-member re-exports that G1 lets through (bare paths where first segment is a workspace member other than self, NOT a top-level module).

G2: derive_attrs is a straight copy of item.attrs.derive (already Vec<String> from extract_attrs). Do NOT re-extract from the AST or call extract_attrs again. The change in indexes.rs is a one-liner: .derive_attrs(item.attrs.derive.clone()).

G2: Same-module scoping is critical. The lookup key in is_derive_companion must use the re-export's module path (e.g., 'mycrate::sub::CellDocument'), not a global search. A pub use of FooBuilder in module bar only checks symbols in module bar.

G2: Lookup key format is 'module_path::prefix' where module_path is the canonical module path (e.g., 'mycrate::sub'). This matches how keys are constructed in indexes.rs: format!("{}::{}", m.path, item.name).

G2: Prefix iteration must start from longest prefix (len(name)) and decrease. Shorter prefixes are less specific — a match on 'Cell' (prefix of 'CellDocumentBuilder') could be a different type. Longest-prefix-first minimizes false suppression.

G2: Private-base-type limitation is a known false negative, not a bug. Private structs with #[derive(bon::Builder)] that generate public builders cannot be suppressed because the base type is absent from the public-only symbol index. Document this in README; do NOT attempt to populate the index with private types.
G3: crate_info.root points to a file (e.g., 'src/lib.rs'), not a directory. Use .parent() to derive the src/ directory. Do NOT use .join("src") — that would produce 'src/lib.rs/src'.

G3: The orphan_file parameter is already workspace-relative (stripped by path.strip_prefix(workspace_root) in check_orphan_files). The derived prefix from crate_info.root.parent() is also workspace-relative. The strip_prefix operation is correct.

G4: Modifying bad-orphan/src/lib.rs to add 'pub mod sub;' must preserve the existing orphan behavior — forgotten.rs must remain undeclared and still appear as an orphan. Verify the existing test_validate_orphan_file_exits_2 still passes after fixture changes.
G4: The deep orphan file (sub/deep/orphan.rs) must NOT be declared in any mod statement. sub/mod.rs declares 'pub mod legal;' but NOT 'pub mod deep;' and NOT 'pub mod deep::orphan;'.

Serde: SymbolEntry uses #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] — the new derive_attrs field will serialize as deriveAttrs. Do NOT add a separate rename annotation. The field-level #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")] is sufficient.
Clippy: cargo clippy -D warnings must remain clean. Fix all warnings; do NOT add #[allow(...)] annotations.

Determinism: All unit test assertions must not depend on HashMap iteration order. Use BTreeMap for ordered collections when iteration order matters in tests. derive_attrs is already sorted by extract_attrs; no new ordering concerns.

groups.description: TASK-G1, TASK-G3, and TASK-G4 touch different physical locations with zero overlap. G1 modifies the check_dead_reexports loop top (lines ~136-142); G3 modifies determine_parent_file body (lines ~106-123, different function); G4 touches tests/fixtures/ and tests/integration_test.rs (different files entirely). All three can be implemented, tested, and committed independently with no merge conflicts.

TASK-G2 modifies check_dead_reexports in the same function body that TASK-G1 touches, and adds the derive_attrs field plumbing. It must run after TASK-G1 lands to avoid merge conflicts on the for-loop body. TASK-README documents the G2 design after implementation is complete. Both tasks are sequentially dependent.
